title: Enhancing Machine Learning Approaches for Graph Optimization Problems with Diversifying Graph Augmentation

problem.claim: Machine-learning approaches are used to solve graph optimization problems, but their performance depends on how training graphs are generated.

gap.claim: Models trained on randomly generated or sampled graphs have limited generalization and perform poorly when test graphs are generated differently.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Learning with Iterative Graph Diversification (LIGD), a framework that iteratively generates diversified training graphs and trains graph-optimization models.
The paper formulates the Diverse Graph Modification Problem (DGMP) for improving training graphs and model performance.
The paper proposes three approaches for solving DGMP that consider model performance and training-graph structural properties.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present LIGD as a new framework and DGMP as a new research problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on well-known graph optimization problems reportedly show significant performance gains for supervised and reinforcement learning approaches.
The proposed approaches reportedly produce near-optimal results.
The proposed approaches reportedly outperform graph augmentation and deep learning-based graph generation baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Machine-learning methods have been proposed for graph optimization problems.
These methods are commonly trained on randomly generated or sampled graphs.
Such training graphs can lead to poor testing performance and limited generalization under mismatched test-graph generation.
LIGD and DGMP are introduced to iteratively diversify training graphs while training graph-optimization models.
Three DGMP approaches are evaluated and are reported to improve performance and produce near-optimal results relative to baselines.

source_observation.claim: Training on graphs generated from a narrow or mismatched distribution can limit test performance.

interpretation.claim: Training-data diversity and alignment with deployment conditions are important for graph machine-learning generalization.

application.claim: Iteratively diversify training graphs while considering both model performance and graph structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which graph distributions, optimization problems, or deployment conditions may not benefit from diversification.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three DGMP algorithms.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated graph optimization problems or datasets.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results, experimental settings, or definitions of near-optimality.
